metas.name: Song of the Sea
metas.description:
Captures a selkie myth drawn the way the sea draws on rock. A mute little girl is the last seal-child; her brother resents her for their mother's death, and the rescue journey is rendered in spirals, knots and watercolour geometry from the studio behind The Secret of Kells lineage.

Ben, a young Irish boy and his little sister, Saoirse, a girl who can turn into a seal, go on an adventure to free the fairies and save the spirit world.

metas.name: Robot Dreams
metas.description:
Captures a friendship conducted entirely without dialogue, in 1980s New York, between a dog and a mail-order robot. They dance to Earth, Wind & Fire on roller skates; a beach closing separates them; the film then does the bravest thing a family film can do with its ending. Wordless, and it earns tears honestly.

The adventures and misfortunes of Dog and Robot in New York City during the 1980s.

metas.name: Marcel the Shell with Shoes On
metas.description:
Captures an inch-high shell with a breadcrumb for a hat, processing fame and loss at full sincerity. A documentarian films his tiny Airbnb cohabitant, whose missing community and ill grandmother turn stop-motion cuteness into something quietly devastating about scale and care.

A cash-strapped documentary maker decides to make his newest documentary about a mollusk shell he finds living in his Airbnb with his friends.

metas.name: Moi, un noir
metas.description:
Captures colonised men narrating themselves as movie stars. Young Nigerien migrants in Abidjan play themselves but dub their own lives in the voices of Edward G. Robinson and Lemmy Caution; documentary subjects seizing the projection and re-authoring what it shows. Ethnography turned inside out, decades before that was a method.

A life of Nigerien immigrants in Abidjan, Ivory Coast within a week.

metas.name: Where Is the Friend's House?
metas.description:
Captures a child's errand at the scale of an epic. A boy takes the wrong notebook home from school and walks to the next village to return it before his friend is expelled; every adult is a locked door. The simplest film on this list and maybe the most suspenseful — proof of your own criterion, that simplicity captures as hard as complexity.

Eight-year-old Ahmed has mistakenly taken his friend Mohammad's notebook. He wants to return it, or else his friend will be expelled from school. The boy determinedly sets out to find Mohammad's home in the neighbouring village.

metas.name: Kuroneko
metas.description:
Captures a ghost story staged like Noh theatre in a bamboo grove. A mother and daughter-in-law, murdered by samurai, return as cat-spirits sworn to drink samurai blood — until one victim is their own son and husband. Mist, wire-work leaps, and vengeance colliding with the vow that powers it.

Two women are raped and killed by samurai soldiers. Soon they reappear as vengeful ghosts who seduce and brutally murder the passing samurai.

metas.name: The Naked Island
metas.description:
Captures a family's whole existence as hauling water uphill. On a barren Seto Inland Sea island with no fresh water, parents row to the mainland and carry buckets up the slope, plant by plant, in near-total silence. Endurance, yes — but filmed as choreography, not punishment; it plays like a folk song about labour.

A family of four are the sole inhabitants of a small island where they struggle each day to irrigate their crops.

metas.name: An Actor's Revenge
metas.description:
Captures kabuki artifice turned into a weapon. An onnagata — a male actor who plays women — hunts the three men who destroyed his parents, never leaving character onstage or off; Ichikawa shoots it in widescreen tableaux where the theatrical sets and the "real" streets obey the same painted logic. Maximalism with a revenge plot for a spine.

Yukinojo, a Kabuki actor, seeks revenge by destroying the three men who caused the deaths of his parents. Also involved are the daughter of one of Yukinojo's targets, two master thieves, and a swordsman who himself is out to kill ...

metas.name: The Swimmer
metas.description:
Captures a suburb revealed one swimming pool at a time. Burt Lancaster, in trunks, decides to "swim home" across the county through his neighbours' pools; each stop strips another layer off the story he's telling about himself. A single afternoon, a single journey, and the observed life turns out to be a projection the whole way.

A man spends a summer day swimming home via all the pools in his quiet suburban neighborhood.

metas.name: Morvern Callar
metas.description:
Captures grief processed through a dead boyfriend's mixtape. A supermarket worker wakes to find he has killed himself, left her his novel's manuscript and a compilation tape; she sends the novel out under her own name and listens her way across Spain. For a man whose taste was mapped through playlists: this is the one where the tape is the character work.

After her beloved boyfriend's suicide, a mourning supermarket worker and her best friend hit the road in Scotland, but find that grief is something that you can't run away from forever.

metas.name: A Tale of the Wind
metas.description:
Captures an 89-year-old filmmaker chasing the one subject that can't be framed. Ivens, making films since 1928 and asthmatic all his life, travels to China to film the wind — waiting with desert nomads, schoolchildren and a terracotta army for the invisible to move something visible. His last film; the hidden structure is weather.

An elderly, asthmatic filmmaker travels to China, hoping to film the wind.

metas.name: Notre musique
metas.description:
Captures a film arranged as Hell, Purgatory, Heaven. Hell is a montage of war footage; Purgatory is a literary conference in Sarajevo where Godard lectures on text and image while Olga, a young journalist, asks the wrong questions; Heaven is a guarded lakeside garden. The middle panel's lecture — shot and reverse-shot as an ethical problem — is the part written for you.

An indictment of modern times divided into three "kingdoms": "Enfer" ("Hell"), "Purgatoire" ("Purgatory") and "Paradis" ("Paradise").

metas.name: The Adventures of Prince Achmed
metas.description:
Captures the Arabian Nights in cut-paper silhouettes, made frame by frame over three years. The oldest animated feature that survives, and it still moves like a shadow-play dream — flying horses, shape-shifting battles, a witch duel in mid-air.

A handsome prince rides a flying horse to faraway lands and embarks on magical adventures, which include befriending a witch, meeting Aladdin, battling demons and falling in love with a princess.

metas.name: Son of the White Mare
metas.description:
Captures a Hungarian folk tale as a full psychedelic cosmology. A hero raised by a white mare descends to the underworld to free three princesses; every frame is saturated folk-art geometry, trees become faces, cities become breasts, colours carry the mythology. The Parajanov lane, in animation.

In this dreamlike Hungarian folk myth, a horse goddess gives birth to three powerful brothers who set out into the Underworld to save three princesses from three evil dragons and reclaim their ancestors' lost kingdom.

metas.name: Night on the Galactic Railroad
metas.description:
Captures two cat schoolboys riding a train through the Milky Way, visiting the dead. Kenji Miyazawa's novel rendered in slow, starlit melancholy; the stops along the line are all the ways people leave. The quietest cosmology in this batch.

Two kittens go on a metaphysical journey on a magical railroad train.

metas.name: Angel's Egg
metas.description:
Captures a girl carrying an egg she will not explain, through a drowned Gothic city, followed by a man carrying a cross-shaped weapon. Almost no dialogue; rain, fossils, water tanks full of shadow fish. Oshii lost his faith and made this instead of a sermon.

A mysterious young girl wanders a desolate, otherworldly landscape, carrying a large egg.

metas.name: Belladonna of Sadness
metas.description:
Captures a medieval witch's rise and destruction in watercolours that keep dissolving. A peasant woman bargains with the Devil across still paintings that pan, bleed and occasionally erupt into full animation and psychedelic rock. Suppressed for decades, restored now — maximalism on paper.

After being raped by an evil feudal lord and subsequently getting banished from her village, a peasant girl makes a pact with the Devil to gain magical powers and take her revenge.

metas.name: Millennium Actress
metas.description:
Captures a retired actress's memories edited as the films she starred in. Two documentary makers interview her, and each recollection deposits them inside the scene — feudal Japan, wartime, a space launch — while her one lost love stays a frame ahead. Your projection framework as a life story: the observed biography keeps re-rendering the hidden one.

A TV interviewer and his cameraman meet a former actress and travel through her memories and career.

metas.name: Ghost in the Shell 2: Innocence
metas.description:
Captures a detective and his mostly-robotic partner investigating murdered dolls that begged to die. Denser and stranger than the first: every character quotes philosophy at each other while the camera orbits ball-jointed gynoids in a festival parade that took a year to animate. The observed/observable problem, with dolls as the transducers.

In the year 2032, Batô, a cyborg detective for the anti-terrorist unit Public Security Section 9, investigates the case of a female robot--one created solely for sexual pleasure--who slaughtered her owner.

metas.name: Inu-Oh
metas.description:
Captures a cursed, contorted Heian-era dancer and a blind biwa player inventing rock concerts in 14th-century Kyoto. Their retellings of the Tales of the Heike make the dead visible to the crowd — and to Inu-Oh himself, whose body straightens as the buried stories get heard. Music as the instrument that reveals the hidden layer; made for you.

A cursed dancer and a musician stun society with electrifying concerts in this animated rock opera.

metas.name: Only Yesterday
metas.description:
Captures a 27-year-old office worker travelling with her 10-year-old self as a permanent passenger. Taeko takes a farm holiday; every adult decision gets cross-examined by the child who wanted fractions explained and a boy to glance at her. Two ages of one person, observing each other, neither in charge.

A twenty-seven-year-old office worker travels to the countryside while reminiscing about her childhood in Tokyo.

metas.name: The Boy and the Heron
metas.description:
Captures a boy following a grey heron into a tower where time pools and the dead curate worlds. Miyazaki's most autobiographical film is also his strangest: warplanes, pelicans, parakeets with knives, and a grand-uncle maintaining a stack of blocks that is either the universe or a career.

In the wake of his mother's death and his father's remarriage, a headstrong boy ventures into a dreamlike world shared by the living and the dead in search of his missing stepmother.

metas.name: Whisper of the Heart
metas.description:
Captures a girl reverse-engineering a boy from the checkout cards in library books. Shizuku notices the same name borrowed every book before her, and the hunt becomes a film about deciding to make things — she writes a novel to find out if she can. The gentlest entry here, and the one about your exact activity: building skill into a position.

A love story between a girl who loves reading books and a boy who has previously checked out all of the library books she chooses.

metas.name: The Red Turtle
metas.description:
Captures a castaway's whole life on one island, without a word of dialogue. A man, a giant red turtle that keeps wrecking his rafts, and then a transformation the film simply places before you like weather. Ghibli co-produced; the water is drawn the way Parajanov drew cloth.

A man is shipwrecked on a deserted island and encounters a big red turtle, which changes his life.

metas.name: When the Wind Blows
metas.description:
Captures a retired couple preparing for nuclear war with government pamphlets and total faith in procedure. Hand-drawn, gentle, funny — Jim keeps saying the authorities know best while the fallout does its work. Raymond Briggs wrote it as a cartoon; it lands like a memorial.

A naive elderly British rural couple survive the initial onslaught of a nuclear war.

metas.name: World of Tomorrow
metas.description:
Captures a little girl visited by her own clone from 227 years later, who explains the future in a level, broken monotone. Seventeen minutes, stick figures, and the whole apparatus of memory-copying, failed immortality and inherited feeling. Your collection's shortest entries are 17 minutes; this is the other one that earns it.

A little girl is taken on a mind-bending tour of her distant future.

metas.name: The Meaning of Life
metas.description:
Captures all of evolution and human history as a twelve-minute time-lapse that refuses to land on us. Creatures morph across geological time, crowds become patterns, patterns become individuals again; the title is the dare, and the ending is the shrug the title earns.

A sprawling look at the evolution of humankind, over the course of a billion years.

metas.name: Everything Will Be OK
metas.description:
Captures Bill, an ordinary man whose days — window light, a cough, a strange feeling in the street — start arriving out of order as an unnamed illness takes his memory apart. Part one of the trilogy; alone, it's the sunniest of the three and the most quietly frightening.

A series of dark and troubling events forces Bill to reckon with the meaning of his life - or lack thereof.

metas.name: I Am So Proud of You
metas.description: Captures Bill's family history told as a hereditary weather system: a mother, a man split into two by a train, a cousin in a rocket, the same darkness handed down like furniture. Part two of the trilogy, and the one where his prose — because by now the narration is prose — peaks.

metas.name: World of Tomorrow Episode Two: The Burden of Other People's Thoughts
metas.description:
Captures little Emily travelling into the mind of her older clone, where memories are stored as literal rooms other people have moved into. The sequel to your #469 goes inward instead of forward: identity as a house full of other people's furniture.

Emily is visited by a backup clone of herself from the even-more distant future, as they must venture into each other's psyches in order to restore the clone's deteriorating mind.

metas.name: World of Tomorrow Episode Three: The Absent Destinations of David Prime
metas.description:
Captures a time-travelling husband erased from his own timeline, sending instructions backward to a wife who no longer remembers him. The most intricate of the three episodes — a love story conducted entirely through messages left in the wrong years.

A hidden memory sends David across the far reaches of time and space to solve a deadly mystery involving his time-traveling future selves.

metas.name: Me
metas.description:
Captures a musical about a self absorbing everything it touches, in twenty-two nearly wordless minutes. His newest: a round character rolls through a hand-drawn world converting people, places and finally the film itself into more of himself. After thirty years of drawing other people's inner lives, this is the one about the ego as a closed system — a transducer with the output looped to the input.

A musical odyssey about generational trauma and the retreat of humanity into itself.
